full_judgment: 2. The short facts giving rise to this rule are that the opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 234 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar District Luximipur against the defendant-opposite parties 2-6 for a permanent injunction stating inter alia that the land described in the schedule to the plaint belonged to the Deity and that the plaintiff has been acting as Sebait of the Deity. The Debttar committee ercted a pucca wall in the Eastern boundary of the 'Kha' Schedule land for profection of the property. But the defendant No.2 issued a notice dated 5.12.85 to the Debottar committee stating that the wall has been created in the 'Gat Schedule land which is Khas land of the Government and directed plaintiffs committee to remove the wall. The Plaintiffs case is that the pucca wall is not within the 'GS schedule land but the that it is within 'Kha' schedule land and that defendant has no right to remove the wall. The plaintiff Deity is not boand to remove that wall which stands in the eastern side of plot No. 2614 of 'Kha' schedule land Hence the suit of permanent injunction restraining the defendants from entering into the suit land and from demolishing the pucca wall.
